title: ginux: connect native fork/exec/threads/waits/pipes to managed supervision
body:
human: Implementation planned by GPT-6.1 Sol high -  implemented and PR submitted by muse spark 1.3 max - reviewed and fixed by GPT-6 astra high.

## Dependency notice (read first)

This branch is stacked directly on `ginux-recipe/g01-launch` (`d1e14bb1`, PR #153, pending review). The diff below therefore includes #153's commits. **Please review only the 6 commits in `d1e14bb1..b3c53518`** (7 files); I will retarget this PR onto `main` once #153 lands. Do not treat the stacked diff as one feature.

## What this does

General native process supervision. On top of the configured launch/result-file loop from #153, it connects the existing managed task model (`ginx-process::ProcessTable`) to the real native supervision loop (`process-native` path):

- fork creates managed parent/child ownership; fixture exit-23/32 rules replaced by `ProcessTable::wait` translation; host pids never exposed.
- libc creation variants: raw `clone`, `vfork`, `clone(CLONE_VM|CLONE_VFORK)` share the managed path; `CLONE_THREAD` and bare `CLONE_VM` denied `ENOSYS`; `clone3` untouched so glibc falls back.
- `execve` / plain `execveat(AT_FDCWD,…,0)` execute under supervision (`TRACEEXEC` + `PTRACE_EVENT_EXEC`, same virtual pid, bumped exec epoch); other `execveat` shapes denied `ENOSYS`.
- Supported `CLONE_THREAD` shape via `clone_thread`; return/parent-tid-cell/`gettid` translated, `getpid` reports tgid; `arch_prctl`/futex/robust/rseq mediated on host; futex-joined thread exit, root exit drains live threads.
- `wait4` fully emulated (blocking park, `WNOHANG`→0, `EINVAL`/`ECHILD`); `kill` forwards SIGTERM/SIGINT/SIGKILL + signal-0 probe; SIGCHLD queued/delivered per child death.
- Supervisor-owned pipe mirror: pipe/pipe2/dup/dup2/dup3/close + fcntl subset; CLOEXEC scrubbed at exec; task death releases ends; teardown audits `live-pipes=0`.

## Demonstration (all supervised, needs root for ptrace/chroot)

```
cargo build -p ginux-init --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu --release
sudo ./target/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/release/ginux process-native config/domain-gate7.toml /tmp/g03-repro/forkstatus   # G03_REPRO: PASS
# .../exec-shell   # SHELL_REPRO: PASS
# .../thread-repro # THREAD_REPRO: PASS (2 threads, join + detach, 7 denials)
# .../wait-repro   # WAIT_REPRO: PASS (exits 42,3; signals 15,9)
# .../pipe-repro   # PIPE_REPRO: PASS (live-pipes=0)
```
Each run also ends `GATE7_NATIVE_PROCESS: PASS`, exit 0, no surviving tracees. Launch-loop side from #153 still intact on the same binary.

## Stated limitations (not fixed here)

- Supervision lives in the `process-native` loop; convergence into the `launch` loop is follow-up work.
- In-tracee SIGCHLD handlers need `rt_sigaction` mediation; job control unmediated.
- Real-libc shell pipelines still need file/memory mediation; acceptance uses raw static stages.
- `clone3`/`chown` denied; hardlinks are content copies.
- One commit also deletes a prohibited `#[cfg(test)]` suite in `ginx-process/src/lib.rs`; kept and flagged rather than separated — happy to split it into a standalone commit on request.

title: feat(init): add configured native launch with faithful completion
body:
human: Implementation planned by GPT-6.1 Sol high -  implemented and PR submitted by muse spark 1.3 max - reviewed and fixed by GPT-6 astra high.

## Summary
Add `ginux launch <config> <root> [--result-file <fresh path>]` to execute a configured native workload with separate stdout and supervisor diagnostics, and report its actual exit code or terminating signal.

## Why
Native execution needs a reusable configuration-driven entry point and an authoritative completion record. Malformed commands, bootstrap failures, result-file failures, and unsupported execution modes must fail explicitly.

## Changes
- Extract launch, supervision, and syscall-dispatch extension points from the demo entry points.
- Add optional `[domain].workdir` (default `/work`, including support for `/`), bounded argv/environment staging, and explicit balanced/ptrace-native validation.
- Reserve result files with O_EXCL before executing a workload; check writes, fsync, and close. Existing result files are preserved. Startup failures return 2; supervision/result failures return 1.
- Preserve workload exit codes and terminating signals, including SIGTRAP; cap audit output and prefix supervisor diagnostics on stderr.
- Close inherited descriptors above stderr, reject alternate syscall ABIs, and deny fork until child ownership is implemented. Unsupported job-control group stops fail without hanging.
- Fix formatting and Clippy failures, and keep the freestanding linker out of Linux host build scripts.
- Add a Linux native launch integration job. Remove unit tests and their runners under the contributing workspace's validation policy; retain the existing required `static-and-unit` status name for compatibility, now running static checks only.

## Testing
- `make check` passes (formatting and Clippy for all production targets).
- `make build build-launch-fixture` passes.
- `sudo make test-launch` passes using real native workloads in temporary chroots: exit codes, signals, arguments, environment, workdir, input limits, unsupported configuration, missing executable, unprivileged bootstrap, descriptor isolation, fork denial, alternate ABI rejection, bounded audit output, result collisions, closed stdout, and an actual result-write failure via RLIMIT_FSIZE.
- Existing config, process, kernel-views, and runtime CLI outputs match the previous PR binary; lifecycle startup and SIGTERM cleanup pass on both. Existing invalid configuration fixtures remain rejected.

## Notes
The launch bootstrap requires host privileges and Linux 5.9+ for close_range, then drops to UID/GID 1000. Only stdio is inherited. Storage/device assignments, networking, resource quota enforcement, native child processes, subsequent exec, and retained-storage generations are outside this launch implementation. `generation` remains null. Config normalization now includes workdir. The complete Rocky VM integration suite has not been rerun.
